title: Contaminated event window: confounding news during event period

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an Event Study approach to isolate the effect of the acquisition from the confounding earnings news. The key assumption is that the market reaction to the acquisition can be identified by controlling for the market return and the earnings surprise. We will use a fixed effects regression model to control for the stock-specific effects and the market return. The coefficient on the event day will capture the abnormal return due to the acquisition.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(plm)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s18_data.csv")

# Convert event_day to a factor variable
data$event_day <- as.factor(data$event_day)

# Create a group variable for each stock
data$stock_id <- as.factor(data$stock_id)

# Run the fixed effects regression
fe_model <- plm(ret ~ event_day + mkt_ret + eps_surprise + 0 | stock_id, data = data, model = "within")

# Print the summary of the regression
summary(fe_model)

# Calculate the robust standard errors
coeftest(fe_model, vcovHC(fe_model, type = "HC1"))

# Plot the event study results
plot(coeftest(fe_model, vcovHC(fe_model, type = "HC1")), xlab = "Event Day", ylab = "Abnormal Return", main = "Event Study Results")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient on the event day to be positive and significant, indicating a positive market reaction to the acquisition announcement. The magnitude of the coefficient will depend on the size and significance of the acquisition. The inclusion of the earnings surprise variable should help control for the confounding effect of the earnings news. The robust standard errors should account for any heteroskedasticity in the data.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with confound adjustment — regress AR on eps_surprise + acquisition dummy
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: After controlling for earnings surprise, acquisition announcement generates negative AR
